intro.say: A volcano is a mountain where hot melted rock comes out. Let us take a look!

rounds.say: Deep inside the Earth it is so hot that rock melts into a runny, glowing liquid.
rounds.caption: melted rock

rounds.say: When the melted rock bursts out of a volcano, we call it lava. This is an eruption!
rounds.caption: lava

options.label: water
options.why: Lava is not water. It is far too hot!

options.label: ice
options.why: Ice is frozen and cold; lava is boiling hot.

rounds.explain: Lava is rock that got so hot it melted into a liquid.

options.label: tree
options.why: A tree grows from the ground; it does not erupt.

options.label: house
options.why: People build houses; a volcano is a mountain.

rounds.explain: A volcano is a mountain with an opening where lava can come out.

options.label: very cold
options.why: Lava is melted rock, so it is hotter than an oven!

rounds.explain: Lava is hot enough to melt rock, much hotter than a fire at home.

rounds.ask: A volcano is erupting. What should people do?

options.label: go closer
options.why: Going near lava is very dangerous.

options.label: touch the lava
options.why: Lava would burn badly; never touch it.

rounds.explain: Lava and ash are dangerous, so people move far away to stay safe.

intro.say: Volcanoes can blow out lava, smoke and ash. Then the lava cools down. Let us see!

rounds.say: In an eruption, melted rock pushes up and out. Lava flows down the sides, and a cloud of ash and smoke rises up.
rounds.caption: eruption

rounds.say: When lava cools, it goes hard. It turns into new rock!
rounds.caption: lava cools into rock

rounds.ask: What happens to lava when it cools down?

options.label: it turns into water
options.why: Lava is rock, so it cannot become water.

options.label: it disappears
options.why: It does not vanish; it stays where it flowed.

rounds.explain: As lava cools it goes hard and becomes new rock.

rounds.ask: What rises into the sky when a volcano erupts?

options.label: rainbows
options.why: Rainbows come from sun and rain, not volcanoes.

options.label: snowflakes
options.why: Volcanoes are hot inside, so they do not blow out snow.

rounds.explain: Erupting volcanoes blow clouds of ash and smoke high into the sky.

rounds.ask: Put the volcano story in order.
rounds.explain: Rock melts deep down, bursts out, flows as lava, then cools into rock.

rounds.ask: Who tells us when it is safe to go near a volcano?

options.label: a friend
options.why: A friend may not know; ask the experts.

options.label: nobody
options.why: Experts watch volcanoes to keep people safe.

rounds.explain: Volcano scientists watch volcanoes closely and warn people about danger.

rounds.ask: Is it part of a volcano eruption?
rounds.explain: Lava, ash and hot rocks come out of volcanoes.

intro.say: Volcanoes can sleep for years, make new islands and even help farms grow. Let us find out how!

rounds.say: Melted rock under the ground is called magma. When it comes out of the volcano, its name changes to lava.
rounds.caption: magma inside, lava outside

rounds.say: Some volcanoes are active and can erupt. Some are sleeping. Others are extinct and will never erupt again.
rounds.caption: active · sleeping · extinct

rounds.say: Volcanoes under the sea can build up rock until it pokes out of the water. That makes a new island!
rounds.caption: new islands

rounds.ask: Melted rock is still deep under the ground. What is it called?

options.label: lava
options.why: We call it lava once it comes out of the volcano.

options.label: sand
options.why: Sand is tiny bits of rock, not melted rock.

rounds.explain: Melted rock under the ground is magma; outside, it is lava.

rounds.ask: A volcano has not erupted for a long time but it could wake up. What kind is it?

options.label: extinct
options.why: Extinct volcanoes can never erupt again.

options.label: erupting
options.why: It is quiet right now, not erupting.

rounds.explain: A sleeping volcano is quiet now but might erupt again one day.

rounds.ask: How can a volcano make a new island?

options.label: Fish build it
options.why: Fish cannot build islands.

options.label: Rain fills it up
options.why: Rain adds water, not land.

rounds.explain: Under-sea lava cools into rock, layer on layer, until land rises above the waves.

rounds.ask: Why do some farmers grow crops near old volcanoes?

options.label: It is always cold
options.why: Being cold does not help crops grow.

options.label: Lava waters plants
options.why: Lava would burn plants, not water them.

rounds.explain: Old volcanic ash breaks down into rich soil that helps plants grow well.

rounds.ask: The ground near a volcano starts to shake and smoke rises. What is the best plan?

options.label: stay to take photos
options.why: Photos are not worth the danger.

options.label: hide in a cave nearby
options.why: Nearby is still too close to the volcano.

rounds.explain: Shaking and smoke can mean an eruption is coming, so follow the warning and leave.
